Cyber Security


84 TanStack npm Packages Compromised in Supply Chain Attack


May 12, 02:44


Attackers published malicious versions of 84 npm packages across the TanStack namespace, targeting CI systems including GitHub Actions with credential-stealing payloads. The compromise affected 42 widely-used TanStack packages with two malicious versions each published around 19:20-19:26 UTC. The attack demonstrates growing threats to JavaScript development supply chains and CI/CD infrastructure.

May 12, 07:29


Security researchers released proof-of-concept exploit code for CVE-2026-0073, a zero-click vulnerability in Android's adbd daemon that allows nearby attackers to gain full shell access without any user interaction. The critical cryptographic flaw was included in Google's May 2026 Android Security Bulletin and affects Android's core system. The vulnerability represents a significant threat to Android device security.

Sources: Cybersecurity News

May 11, 17:54

The attacks deploy a backdoor called Filemanager on compromised web hosting servers worldwide. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain elevated control without credentials.

May 12, 04:12


A new tool called BitUnlocker exploits a downgrade attack against Microsoft's BitLocker encryption, allowing attackers with physical access to decrypt protected volumes on patched Windows 11 machines. The attack exploits CVE-2025-48804 and takes advantage of the gap between patching and certificate revocation. The tool demonstrates practical exploitation of critical zero-day vulnerabilities in Windows encryption.
